absent: Width-specific SMM state-save helpers and SMRAM offset validation logic.
Contracts and failure modes of platform hooks for SMM enter and leave, NMI mask handling, interrupt shadow, control registers, descriptor tables, EFER, and unhandleable-emulation detection.
Semantics of segment, debug-register, control-register, flags, instruction-pointer, CPUID-dirty, MMU-reset, nested-mode and guest-memory access helpers.
Meaning and propagation of VM-dead flag and all-CPU request mechanism.
Layout and lifetime of AVIC VM data hash table, VM identifier allocation and wrap recovery, and effect of force enable flag.
Sources of x2AVIC enablement and maximum physical identifier values and APIC mode helpers.
SVM intercept numbering, MSR bitmap helpers, MSR filter policy, nested intercept recalculation, and TLB-flush request handling.
Log prefix macro and include-guard constant beyond their declarative role.

findings.text: SMM entry, SMM exit emulation, and SVM MSR intercept control are non-static interfaces usable across files; the first two manage handler activation and return while the third adjusts per-vCPU MSR interception state.

SMM entry chooses a width-specific in-memory save image by long-mode capability, starts from a cleared image, asks platform code to leave guest mode, announces SMM activation, persists the image into guest memory, then establishes handler execution context; save, hook, store, or debug-control failures terminate the VM.

SMM activation converges on an isolated handler context with fixed flags, fixed entry address, no interrupt shadow, reduced paging and protection controls, cleared extended controls and descriptor-table location, fixed debug control, flat descriptors derived from SMBASE, cleared extended feature state on 64-bit-capable guests, and refreshed CPUID and MMU tracking.
The SMRAM image is zero-initialized before selective population and moved as one fixed-size block between host memory and guest memory at a fixed offset from SMBASE on both entry and exit.

SMM exit reads the saved image from guest memory, restores NMI masking unless already inside NMI, clears SMM-active notification, descends to a safe real-mode-like state with ordered paging, protection, and long-mode teardown, invokes the platform leave hook before loading saved state, then delegates to the width-specific loader and leaves nested guest mode if restoration fails there.

RSM protected-mode restoration preserves paging-identifier low bits while PCID enable is temporarily off, programs paging base and control registers in an order that satisfies PAE and PCID constraints, then restores PCID enable and identifier bits when requested; rejected control updates abort emulation as unhandleable.

32-bit RSM restoration covers flags with fixed bit forced, instruction pointer, eight general registers, two debug registers, system and segment descriptors with separately stored selectors, both descriptor tables, SMBASE, control registers through the protected-mode helper, and saved interruptibility after clearing current shadow.

64-bit RSM restoration covers sixteen general registers from reversed storage, instruction pointer and flags with fixed bit forced, two debug registers, SMBASE, extended feature state without active long-mode indication, system and segment descriptors, descriptor tables, control registers, interruptibility, and shadow-stack pointer when that feature is present; rejected updates abort as unhandleable.
The 32-bit segment save entry is a packed record of three 32-bit values describing attribute flags, limit, and base.

The 32-bit SMRAM image is a packed record with reserved prologue, SMBASE and revision, restart controls, saved extended control state, interrupt-shadow extension with padding, ordered segment and table save entries, separate selector words, debug state, general registers in natural order, and instruction, flag, paging-base, and control state.
The 64-bit segment save entry combines two 16-bit selector and attribute fields with a 32-bit limit and a 64-bit base.

The 64-bit SMRAM image starts with segment and table entries, followed by restart controls and shadow state, extended feature state, SVM guest tracking, revision and SMBASE with reserved words, shadow-stack pointer, unimplemented SVM host saves, and control, debug, flag, instruction, and reversed-order general-register state.
The unified SMRAM container overlays the 32-bit image, the 64-bit image, and a raw fixed-length byte view.
SMM handler entry uses instruction pointer 0x8000, and the SMRAM image occupies 512 bytes at SMBASE plus 0xfe00.

SMM entry disables protection, emulation, task-switched, and paging controls, zeroes the extended control register and extended feature register on capable guests, forces fixed flag and debug-control values, and zeroes interrupt-table base and limit.

Saved descriptor flags decode distinct bit fields into granularity, size, long, availability, presence, privilege, descriptor kind, and type attributes, with unusable derived as absence of present and padding cleared.

Segment installation combines a caller-supplied selector with saved base, limit, and decoded flags in the 32-bit case, and uses saved selector, limit, base, and shifted attribute data in the 64-bit case.

The AVIC guest tag places a masked VM identifier above the vCPU-index bit width and a masked vCPU index in the low bits, with extraction helpers for each field and a constructor that checks round-trip preservation.

AVIC mode control maps a textual automatic keyword to a negative sentinel, reports that sentinel as a negative boolean display value, otherwise delegates to boolean parameter helpers, and defaults to automatic mode.

AVIC retains separate automatic and force controls, a fixed hash-width constant, a monotonic VM identifier counter with wrap indicator, and cached x2AVIC enablement plus maximum physical identifier state.
AVIC declares a dedicated spinlock for the VM data hash beside the VM identifier allocator state.

x2APIC MSR interception handling is idempotent against cached state and inactive when x2AVIC support is off; otherwise it toggles read tracking over the readable x2APIC range and write tracking for priority, completion, self-delivery, and command registers, then records the new state.

MSR intercept updates honor userspace read and write filter allowances when clearing tracking, otherwise set tracking, and unconditionally mark nested enlightenment state dirty while requesting nested bitmap recalculation.
The vendor vCPU structure is obtained from the generic vCPU pointer through enclosing-structure derivation.

VMCB cleanliness tracking clears the selected control bit, while nested-enlightenment dirty handling marks that area only when the corresponding MSR-bitmap enlightenment is active; an alternate build provides an empty operation.

The effective AVIC physical identifier ceiling is the smaller of the VM-configured identifier capacity minus one and the architecture ceiling chosen by x2AVIC enablement and guest APIC mode, using the largest ceiling when no vCPU context is supplied.

AVIC activation clears enable and extended-mode controls, programs the physical-identifier ceiling, enables acceleration, drops CR8-write interception, requests a current-CPU TLB flush to cover backing-page aliasing, then selects extended mode with relaxed MSR interception for x2APIC guests or strict interception otherwise.
Clearing an SVM intercept updates the primary control bitmap, marks intercept state dirty, and recalculates nested intercepts when a nested guest is active.
SMM entry failures after partial mutation terminate the whole VM, including failure to establish the fixed debug control value.

Because the nested leave hook runs before saved-state loading, a failed return to a nested guest may already be in guest mode, so the failure path explicitly exits nesting to deliver shutdown at the architecturally correct level.
